_readme: Expert-default signal for scripts/derive-signals.mjs's `families` calibration in assets/decide.mjs: which models a real tool actually ships/recommends as its own default or featured roster for a given task, curled as static HTML/text 2026-09-07 (raw pages saved alongside the research batch that built this). A model counts as an expert default for a task when a source below explicitly names it for that task; membership counts the same regardless of source (a vendor publishing a shortlist, not a ranked table) — this mirrors eval/METHOD.md's family-(c) treatment. Disclosed bias: 2 of the 3 usable sources are Anthropic's own documentation (Claude Code, Anthropic's own model-selection guide) — OpenAI's (platform.openai.com/docs/guides/model-selection), Google's (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models) and GitHub Copilot's (docs.github.com/copilot) equivalent pages were fetched but are client-rendered SPAs; curl returned nav/CSS/sidebar only, no usable guidance text, despite retries — so this family under-represents OpenAI/Google/Copilot relative to Anthropic. That is exactly why the calibration rule this file feeds never lets 'expert_default' alone satisfy the >=2-family bar — it always needs a second, non-Anthropic-authored family (usage or arena) to actually promote a model to 'strong'. Refresh: re-curl each source_url, diff for a changed roster/matrix, replace the affected `sources[].entries`, bump `as_of`.

sources.note: Cursor's featured/first-class model roster (each with its own doc page). Cursor doesn't break this down per-task, so every listed model is credited for the three task types its own docs frame this roster around: coding, agents, frontend. Composer 2.5 (Cursor's own model) is not in the 67-model catalog and is left unmapped.

Model aliases and their stated purpose: 'sonnet' -> Sonnet 5 ('daily coding tasks'), 'opus' -> Opus 5 ('complex reasoning tasks'), 'fable' -> Fable 5.1 ('hardest and longest-running tasks'), 'haiku' -> Haiku 4.5 ('fast and efficient...simple tasks'). Task credit given only where the source text names a task this product's taxonomy has a match for (see the Anthropic 'choosing a model' source below for Opus/Sonnet/Haiku's fuller task lists — this entry only adds what Claude Code's own docs/blog state that source doesn't already cover: the long-horizon-agentic framing for Fable).

Anthropic's own need -> model -> example-use-cases selection matrix. Verbatim task framing: Fable 5.1 = 'highest available capability' / 'agent sessions that run for hours, multistep deep research, analysis carried through to a finished document'; Opus 5 = 'complex agentic coding and enterprise work' / 'multihour autonomous coding agents...vision-heavy workflows, computer use'; Sonnet 5 = 'speed and capability for everyday coding, agent, and enterprise workloads' / 'code generation, data analysis, content creation, visual understanding, agentic tool use'; Haiku 4.5 = 'lowest latency and price' / 'real-time applications, high-volume intelligent processing, cost-sensitive deployments, sub-agent tasks'.
